prior_findings.title: reclaim reorders POST tasks but durable cohort_members stays stale
prior_findings.evidence: file_orchestration_journal.py:3149-3159 — inside reclaim_pipeline_job_reservation's _locked_cycle_write, the forcing branch now mints the per-attempt comment AND persists row['cohort_members'] = list(request_row['cohort_members']) gated on forcing_member_identity_is_complete(request_row); request_row passed through the same _bounded_cohort_members normalization as the original reserve, and completeness is checked on that exact normalized row, so durable bytes == validated request bytes. Backfill loop at :3188-3198 explicitly skips cohort_members for forcing_reclaim, making :3159 the single writer. Red/green proof pair: node27-reclaim-order-probe.txt exit=1 (sent [model_1,model_0] vs durable [model_0,model_1], committed in the fix commit) vs node27-reclaim-order-green.txt exit=0 (durable now [model_1,model_0]). Regression test test_permitted_reclaim_persists_current_attempt_task_mapping_before_post (tests/test_forcing_submit_ambiguity.py:840) drives the real seam end-to-end: real FileOrchestrationJournalRepository, real HttpSlurmGatewayClient returning 502, real reconcile_reserved_unbound_jobs permit path with coverage-complete absence at anchor+3min (>120s grace), second _submit_and_wait_cycle_stage with reversed basins; asserts same pipeline_job_id, submission_attempt==2, exactly 2 POSTs, sent task order == durable cohort_members order. Reachability of the conditional's false branch checked: the only production forcing caller (_reserve_cycle_stage, chain_forecast_orchestrator_cycle.py:705-751) validates forcing_member_identity_is_complete on the same evidence and raises FORCING_SUBMIT_IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE before reserve_candidate; reserve_candidate is the sole reclaim entry; FileOrchestrationJournalRepository is the only repo with supports_accepted_submit_reconcile=True (chain_repository.py's SQL reclaim lacks the entire forcing identity surface, so R2-A never existed there).

prior_findings.title: unshipped pre-token compatibility shim + legacy test removal
prior_findings.evidence: forcing_submit_identity.py: legacy slurm_comment_for acceptance deleted (import gone; is_current_forcing_attempt_comment is now the sole comment gate). reconcile.py: _query_forcing_controller_identity's attempt_anchor/query_end/current_attempt_comment params and the SubmitTime-window branch deleted; identity tuple fixed at (user,account,job_name). No dangling references: no test/source references to removed kwargs, legacy_comment, or the deleted test; _parse_fallback_submit_instant/_fallback_candidate_in_window remain only for the pre-existing #1565 forecast name-window fallback (:535-539) and candidate submitted_at reporting (:727). Fail-closed preserved by construction: pre-token rows now fail forcing_member_identity_is_complete → _forcing_submit_reconcile_job False (reconcile.py:1782-1784) → generic pre-#2447 path, which on a comment-less cluster raises ReconcileQueryUnavailable (held, never absence, never retry); typed bind/permit CASes both gate on forcing_submit_identity_is_complete (journal:3279/3283, 3362/3366) so legacy rows can neither bind nor be released through the new machinery. Legacy test was replaced (not dropped) by the reclaim regression test; spec scenario 'sparse historical failed row' remains covered by test_sparse_historical_forcing_failure_does_not_block_a_new_successful_attempt.
